stem: A 32-year-old male presents with rapidly progressive renal failure and hemoptysis. Renal biopsy reveals necrotizing crescentic glomerulonephritis with smooth linear IgG staining along the glomerular capillary walls. Autoantibody testing confirms anti-glomerular basement membrane (anti-GBM) disease. Which of the following specific molecular domains serves as the primary autoantigenic target in this condition?

options.text: The N-terminal 7S domain of the alpha-1 chain of Type IV collagen [alpha1(IV)]
The non-collagenous domain 1 of the alpha-3 chain of Type IV collagen [alpha3(IV)NC1]
The triple-helical domain of the alpha-5 chain of Type IV collagen [alpha5(IV)]
The C-terminal domain of agrin and perlecan proteoglycans

stem: A renal biopsy is performed on a patient presenting with acute anuric renal failure. Direct immunofluorescence (DIF) staining of frozen native kidney tissue is evaluated. Which of the following DIF patterns is pathognomonic for anti-GBM glomerulonephritis?

options.text: Continuous, smooth, ribbon-like linear IgG staining along the glomerular capillary loops
Coarse, lumpy-bumpy granular IgG and C3 deposition along the subepithelial space
Pauci-immune staining with absence or trace (< 2+) immune complex deposits
'Full-house' immunofluorescence with heavy IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, and C1q mesangial deposits

stem: Which of the following ultrastructural findings on electron microscopy (EM) best characterizes native kidney biopsy specimens in patients with pure anti-GBM disease?

options.text: Subepithelial humps with extensive podocyte effacement
Subendothelial wire-loop electron-dense deposits
Fibrin tactoids in Bowman space with ABSENCE of discrete electron-dense deposits
Intramembranous ribbon-like extremely dense deposits along the lamina densa

stem: A 25-year-old male active smoker presents with 3 days of severe dyspnea, gross hemoptysis, and acute oligo-anuric renal failure. Urinalysis shows 3+ protein, dysmorphic RBCs, and RBC casts. Which bedside diagnostic test provides the fastest non-invasive indication of active pulmonary hemorrhage in this setting?

options.text: High-resolution computed tomography (HRCT) of the chest without contrast
Arterial blood gas (ABG) showing acute metabolic acidosis
Sputum cytology showing eosinophils and Charcot-Leyden crystals
Single-breath Carbon Monoxide Diffusing Capacity (DLCO) demonstrating a > 30% increase above baseline

stem: Which of the following clinical and histological parameters at initial presentation carries the worst prognosis for renal function recovery in patients diagnosed with anti-GBM disease?

options.text: Serum creatinine > 5.7 mg/dL (500 umol/L), oligo-anuria, and 100% cellular crescents on biopsy
Presence of frank hemoptysis and bilateral pulmonary alveolar infiltrates
Positive serum anti-GBM antibody titer measured by indirect immunofluorescence
Age under 40 years with underlying HLA-DRB1*1501 genotype

stem: According to the KDIGO 2024 Clinical Practice Guidelines, what is the primary therapeutic mechanism and rationale for initiating therapeutic plasmapheresis (plasma exchange) immediately upon diagnosis of anti-GBM disease?

options.text: Suppression of interleukin-6 and tumor necrosis factor-alpha gene transcription
Depletion of circulating CD20-positive B-lymphocytes within 48 hours
Rapid mechanical clearance of circulating pathogenic anti-GBM IgG autoantibodies
Replenishment of deficient Complement Factor H and Factor I regulating proteins

stem: Which of the following therapeutic regimens represents the standard initial triple-therapy induction protocol recommended by KDIGO for non-dialysis dependent patients with acute anti-GBM glomerulonephritis?

options.text: High-dose Mycophenolate Mofetil + Oral Prednisone + Belimumab
Daily/alternate-day Plasmapheresis + Oral Cyclophosphamide + Pulse IV Methylprednisolone followed by oral Prednisone
Continuous Venovenous Hemofiltration + IV Cyclosporine A + Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG)
Eculizumab + High-dose Tacrolimus + Oral Prednisone

stem: A 28-year-old female diagnosed with acute anti-GBM disease requires induction therapy. However, she strongly desires future fertility and refuses cyclophosphamide due to gonadotoxicity. According to KDIGO recommendations, which alternative agent can be substituted for cyclophosphamide in combination with plasmapheresis and corticosteroids?

options.text: Azathioprine
Methotrexate
Tacrolimus
Rituximab

stem: A 68-year-old male presents with severe acute renal failure requiring hemodialysis on presentation. Kidney biopsy shows 100% cellular crescents with linear IgG deposition. He has NO shortness of breath, NO cough, and chest X-ray is entirely clear. Serum anti-GBM titer is positive. What is the most appropriate management regarding immunosuppressive therapy according to KDIGO guidelines?

options.text: Withhold intensive immunosuppression and plasmapheresis because kidney recovery rate is < 5% and infection risks outweigh benefits
Initiate urgent daily plasmapheresis and high-dose cyclophosphamide immediately
Administer high-dose pulse methylprednisolone monotherapy without plasmapheresis
Perform emergency bilateral nephrectomy to stop antibody production

stem: A 58-year-old female is diagnosed with rapidly progressive glomerulonephritis. Serologic testing demonstrates high titers of BOTH anti-GBM antibodies and MPO-ANCA (double-positive disease). How does the long-term clinical behavior and management of double-positive disease differ from classic single-positive anti-GBM disease?

options.text: Double-positive patients have a milder acute presentation and do not require acute plasmapheresis
Double-positive patients never develop pulmonary hemorrhage and can be treated with prednisone alone
Double-positive patients present acutely like anti-GBM disease, but carry a HIGH RELAPSE RISK like ANCA vasculitis, requiring long-term maintenance immunosuppression
Double-positive patients have a 100% cure rate after 2 weeks of oral cyclophosphamide

stem: A 24-year-old male with X-linked Alport syndrome due to a pathogenic COL4A5 mutation undergoes living donor kidney transplantation. Nine months post-transplant, he develops graft dysfunction, microhematuria, and proteinuria. Allograft biopsy reveals linear IgG staining along the donor GBM. What is the fundamental pathophysiological mechanism of this post-transplant complication?

options.text: Recurrence of native Alport basement membrane thinning within the donor kidney
Development of de novo anti-GBM antibodies by the recipient immune system reacting against normal alpha3/4/5(IV) collagen chains present in the donor allograft
Acute calcineurin inhibitor nephrotoxicity causing endothelial ballooning
Transmission of donor pre-existing anti-GBM antibodies during organ procurement

stem: Which environmental risk factor has been most consistently identified as a potent precipitant specifically for pulmonary alveolar hemorrhage in patients circulating anti-GBM autoantibodies?

options.text: High dietary sodium intake
Chronic exposure to ultraviolet B radiation
Recent administration of recombinant erythropoietin
Active cigarette smoking or heavy hydrocarbon solvent inhalation

stem: When evaluating light microscopy of renal biopsies from patients with acute anti-GBM disease, which feature regarding crescent formation distinguishes anti-GBM disease from ANCA-associated vasculitis?

options.text: Crescents in anti-GBM disease are characteristically synchronous (all crescents are at the same stage of cellular evolution)
Crescents in anti-GBM disease are always asynchronous, showing mixed cellular and fibrous stages
Anti-GBM disease never produces cellular crescents, showing only ischemic tubular atrophy
Anti-GBM disease presents exclusively with granulomatous vasculitis in interlobar arteries

stem: A 40-year-old male with confirmed anti-GBM disease undergoes routine serologic workup. What is the expected serum complement profile (C3 and C4 levels) in uncomplicated, pure anti-GBM disease?

options.text: Severely depressed C3 with normal C4 levels
Severely depressed C4 with normal C3 levels
Normal serum C3 and normal serum C4 levels
Marked reduction of both C3 and C4 to near zero

stem: Which of the following lab parameters is considered the gold standard for monitoring therapeutic response and deciding when to discontinue plasmapheresis in anti-GBM disease?

options.text: Normalization of serum creatinine and blood urea nitrogen
Serial quantitative anti-GBM antibody titers measured by ELISA becoming negative
Complete disappearance of microscopic hematuria on urinalysis
Recovery of normal 24-hour urine volume > 2000 mL

stem: During plasma exchange for active anti-GBM disease with co-existing pulmonary hemorrhage, what replacement fluid should be utilized towards the end of the session to prevent bleeding complications?

options.text: Fresh Frozen Plasma (FFP) to replenish clotting factors depleted during exchange
100% Normal Saline without protein supplementation
Hydroxyethyl starch (HES) colloid solution
Packed Red Blood Cells (PRBCs) suspended in dextrose

stem: A 35-year-old male with end-stage kidney disease secondary to anti-GBM disease has been stable on hemodialysis. He is being evaluated for kidney transplantation. What is the minimum recommended waiting period after circulating anti-GBM antibodies become persistently undetectable before proceeding with renal transplantation?

options.text: 1 week after initial hemodialysis session
1 month after stopping cyclophosphamide
3 months regardless of anti-GBM antibody titers
At least 6 months of persistent seronegativity for anti-GBM antibodies

stem: Which of the following immunopathologic features on renal biopsy definitive distinguishes anti-GBM disease from ANCA-associated vasculitis in a patient presenting with pulmonary-renal syndrome?

options.text: Presence of cellular crescents in > 50% of glomeruli
Presence of fibrinoid necrosis within capillary loops
Linear continuous IgG immunofluorescence along GBM in anti-GBM disease vs. pauci-immune IF in ANCA vasculitis
Presence of interstitial red blood cell accumulation
